Clear urine can be a normal finding, but it can also be a sign of various conditions. The color of urine is influenced by the concentration of waste products, such as urea, creatinine, and bilirubin, as well as the presence of certain substances like glucose, ketones, and myoglobin [1]. 

In a well-hydrated individual, urine is typically pale yellow or clear due to the high water content [2]. However, if the urine is consistently clear, it may indicate that the kidneys are not concentrating the urine properly, which can be a sign of kidney disease or diabetes insipidus [3].

On the other hand, clear urine can also be a sign of a low concentration of waste products, which can be seen in individuals with a low-protein diet or those who are taking certain medications, such as diuretics [4]. Additionally, certain medical conditions, such as liver disease or a urinary tract infection, can also cause clear urine [5].

It is essential to note that clear urine can also be a normal finding in individuals who are taking certain medications, such as certain antibiotics or antihistamines [6].
